rounds.response: This packet means your landlord has filed a lawsuit to evict you (called an Unlawful Detainer); the Summons tells you the court has opened the case and lists a deadline to respond and a hearing date. An “answer” is your formal written response to the landlord’s claims — the summons will show the exact deadline and how to file — if you don’t file by the deadline the landlord can ask the court for a default judgment which may lead to eviction. Right now, read the summons for the exact dates, make copies, and gather key documents (lease, rent receipts, notices, texts/emails, and ID). You should file and serve your answer (or ask the court for more time if allowed) before the deadline, and plan to attend the hearing; if you need help with forms, contact the courthouse self‑help center, local legal aid or tenant‑defense clinic. If you tell me the county and state, I can point to the typical local forms and where to file them.

rounds.response: Many courts have a specific “Answer — Unlawful Detainer” form (or a standard civil answer); the clerk or court self‑help desk can tell you the exact form or whether a handwritten response is allowed. Courts usually charge a filing fee but offer a fee‑waiver (form for inability to pay) — ask the clerk and bring ID and proof of income/benefits. After you file, you must “serve” a copy on the landlord (or their attorney) by an approved method — often personal delivery by someone over 18 who is not you, or mail if local rules allow — the summons or clerk can say which methods and timing are required. Because your deadline is in about three days, go to the courthouse clerk or self‑help center today with the summons, complaint, lease, rent receipts and ID so they can provide the right form, accept your filing, or help you fill out a fee‑waiver. If you give your county and state I can point you to the local answer form and clerk contact/website.
